lesson.subtitle: Lesson 2 -- The Welcome Pack: Reading What the School Sends You
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Laís Paludetto Rodrigues | Lesson 2 -- The Welcome Pack

listenings.text: Hi Lais, it's Beatriz. Your mum gave the school my number because I did the same programme last year, so here is everything I wish somebody had told me. First, the paperwork. I sent my documents three weeks before I flew and I still ran out of time, so start now. Second, the transit pass. I didn't buy one in the first week because I thought my host family would drive me everywhere, and that was a mistake. Get it on day one. And third, orientation. I have never been so lost as I was that morning, mostly because I arrived exactly on time instead of early. Go early, find the hall, and then go and get a coffee. Message me whenever you want, honestly.

Hello, this is Peter Novak from the international student office. I'm calling about your file. I've received your school letter from Brazil and your passport copy, so those are done, thank you. There are two things still missing. The medical form has not arrived yet, and the deadline for that one is the Friday before classes start, so please ask your parents to send it this week. The second thing is the photo for your student card. You uploaded one last month, but it was too dark for the system to accept, so I'm afraid we need another one. Everything else looks great. See you at orientation.

extra_audio.text: The welcome letter arrives by email six weeks before the flight. Lais reads it and makes a list of every document the school asks for. She fills out the medical form and her father signs it. The school office confirms that the paperwork has arrived. On the first Monday she goes to orientation and picks up her student card.

reading.rtitle: Welcome to the Burnaby International Programme
paras: Dear Lais, welcome. We received your application in June and the placement committee confirmed your host family last week, so the hardest part is already behind you. This letter tells you what is still open and what happens in your first days here.

Paperwork. We have already received your school letter and your passport copy. We have not received the medical form yet, and that one is mandatory before the first day of class. Please also fill out the emergency contact sheet, which is attached to this email. Last year several students sent it in September and missed the deadline for the school insurance.

Orientation. Orientation is on the first Monday of the term, at nine, in the main hall. You will meet the international counsellor, you will get your timetable and your student card, and somebody from the buddy programme will show you the facilities. It usually finishes around one o'clock.

Getting around. Most of our students buy a transit pass in the first week, because the bus is the fastest way to school from your neighbourhood. You can sign up for it online, but you have to do it in person the first time, with your student card. Bring a jacket. It has rained every September since we opened this programme.
reading.source: Email -- Burnaby School District, International Programme

You are at the counter and you want the transit pass. Say what you want and what you have with you.

items.situation: Somebody asks if you have ever lived abroad before. Answer honestly and add one detail.
tips: I travelled to Europe with my mum last year.

items.situation: You missed a deadline by one day. Explain what happened without making a drama of it.
tips: I'm sorry, I sent it yesterday.
I didn't see the email until Friday.
